routes.label: Use the radii as lengths along the hypotenuse

question:
In right \(\triangle ABC\) with legs \(5\) and \(12,\) arcs of circles are drawn, one with center \(A\) and radius \(12,\) the other with center \(B\) and radius \(5.\) They intersect the hypotenuse in \(M\) and \(N.\) Then \(MN\) has length

[Figure 1](figures/1985_AMC_12_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The arcs give two distances along the hypotenuse: \(AM=12\), because \(M\) lies on the circle centered at \(A\), and \(BN=5\), because \(N\) lies on the circle centered at \(B\). Finding the whole hypotenuse will let us compare these distances.

Since the triangle is right with legs \(5\) and \(12\), the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AB=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{169}=13.
\]
Thus \(AN=AB-BN=13-5=8\). Both intersection points lie on segment \(AB\), and \(AN=8<AM=12<AB=13\), so their order is \(A,N,M,B\). Therefore
\[
MN=AM-AN=12-8=\boxed{4},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
